interpretations.rationale: Review revision answering the gaps raised by the correction to behaviour entry ee850f515b5d49718d5f55c4c1d36e61-knowledge-0. Receipt e3bd14fe94534fbca3955cae4e521df7 (experiment be2af26c5f2f43679ffe2592668f8388-experiment) supplied the measurement: a real three-node network, leader 1 elected with committed 1 and committedEntryInCurrentTerm true, then isolated from both followers, admitted 32 same-context requests as unconfirmed 32 with confirmed 0 while still StateLeader and emitted 64 heartbeat messages; its comparisons hold with complete admissions. Re-reading each recorded use against revision 2: the growth, retention, drain-burst, CheckQuorum-control and byte-measurement accounts depend on per-request, context-blind admission and on retained caller-supplied state, none of which the correction touches; the amplification statement is the only affected element and is now stricter and measured, one heartbeat per other tracked peer per retry, so the figure rises with the voter count. Nothing in the asserted defect changes: the library still imposes no bound on accepted read requests, still never reclaims the queue within a process lifetime, and still emits retry-proportional traffic. Boundaries unchanged: severity is measured for retained payload and heartbeat count only, the partition is modelled with the network helper's isolation rather than a real transport, footprint and liveness are unclaimed, and etcd's own retry policy is unexamined.
limitations: Source and receipt-reading review only; no new execution is claimed for this answer.
The corrected figure is measured in one three-voter configuration at one depth (32 requests), so the per-peer scaling is inferred from the broadcast loop plus that single measurement.

The remaining boundaries listed for the underlying question are unchanged: measured payload and heartbeat counts only, modelled isolation, process-lifetime bound, and no examination of etcd's retry policy.
